desk.headline: Revenue up 9.2% to $2.18bn, slightly below estimates; low river water hit profit (adjusted EPS $1.11 vs $1.20); 2027 yield goal trimmed

numbers.eps_basis: adjusted diluted (non-GAAP); GAAP diluted EPS $1.11 vs $1.15

other.label: 2027 season advance bookings
other.change: +17% vs 2026 season at same point; 68% sold

results: Revenue grew 9.2% to $2.18bn as more ships sailed (capacity +10.2%), but low water on some European rivers forced cancellations, costing about $100m of revenue.
Occupancy dropped to 91.3% from 96.0% and net yield slipped 0.8% to $612 per passenger day; adjusted EBITDA fell 4.3% to $673.5m.
Net income attributable to shareholders fell to $496.9m from $514.1m; adjusted EPS was $1.11 against $1.20 a year ago.
Bookings stay strong: the 2027 season is 68% sold with $5.83bn booked, 17% ahead of 2026 at the same point, on 15% more capacity.
Cash stood at $4.1bn and Viking bought back $350m of shares in the quarter, its first buyback under a new $1.0bn programme.

guidance.summary: Viking gives no formal financial guidance in its release. On the call, management trimmed its 2027 net yield growth goal to low-to-mid single digits from mid-single digits, mainly because goodwill cruise vouchers handed to affected river guests will be used on 2027 sailings.

points: About 70% of river capacity days in the quarter were affected by low water; management said it is too early to size the Q4 hit, though recent rain has helped.
Roughly $165m of cancellation vouchers and $265m of goodwill vouchers were issued; many guests have rebooked, mostly for 2027 river trips.
Ocean cruises are 77% sold for 2027 at higher prices ($873 vs $785 per day), seen as a sign of healthy demand.
Net leverage was 1.2 times; buybacks will continue under the $1.0bn programme with no fixed timetable.
Fleet growth continues, with options secured for 10 more European river ships and 4 ocean ships.
call.source: Press release (6-K Exhibit 99.1) and The Motley Fool call transcript, 17 Nov 2026

watch: How much the low-water disruption and voucher use weigh on Q4 and 2027 river yields.
Occupancy recovery back toward the mid-90s.
Pace of share buybacks under the $1.0bn programme.
